license: BSD-3-Clause for source-derived code and literals
method: Direct header, implementation and class-test audit; no C++ build or execution. The transport is injected behind a trait so that every expectation is checked against a recorded response: no test in this group opens a socket, performs a DNS lookup, or contacts the OpenMS REST server.
evidence_tier: tier 3 (source review, transcribed class-test expectations and OpenMS's own string literals) and tier 4 (expectations derived from the implementations - the 400 status boundary, the StringUtils::toInt32 conversion rules, the non-transitivity of VersionDetails::operator<, the strict 24-hour comparison, the collision-suffix sequence - plus the native bounds)

source_surface.counting_rule: Public declarations in the four headers, constructors and destructors counted separately: CurlInit::ensure (1) plus its private ctor/dtor and two deleted copy members, which are not public; NetworkGetRequest ctor, dtor, setUrl, setTimeout, run, getResponse, getResponseBinary, hasError, getErrorString (9); Network::downloadFile (1); UpdateCheck::run (1). The class-test total is 9 (NetworkGetRequest) + 1 (Network) + 1 (UpdateCheck); CurlInit has no class test in the SDK.

source_anchors.operation: CurlInit is documented as a thread-safe RAII guard whose ensure() must be called before any curl API; ureq has no global state, so nothing is ported
ensure() relies on the C++11 guarantee that a function-local static is constructed exactly once, even under concurrent first calls, and destroyed at process exit
the header states that the instance is reusable, that each run replaces the previously observed state, and that redirects are followed automatically
writeCallback inserts size * nmemb bytes into an unbounded std::vector<char>, so the peer decides how much memory the process commits
CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is set to 1 and CURLOPT_MAXREDIRS is never set, so the redirect chain is libcurl's unlimited default; the port caps it at 10 and reports TooManyRedirects
CURLOPT_NOSIGNAL is set to 1 for a thread-safe DNS timeout; ureq installs no signal handler, so there is nothing to disable
CURLOPT_TIMEOUT is set only when timeout_ > 0, so 0 and any negative value leave the request without a deadline

the status is read only after curl_easy_perform succeeded, by which point the write callback has already stored the body; an HTTP error therefore sets has_error_ while getResponse still returns the error document, which is why the port sets ureq's http_status_as_error to false
the error string for a status failure is "HTTP error " + std::to_string(http_code), formed in OpenMS code rather than libcurl, so it is reproduced byte for byte
saveFileName_ cuts at the first '?' before cutting at the first '#', so a '#' inside a query string is already gone when the fragment is looked for

the basename comes from std::filesystem::path::filename, which treats '\' as a separator on Windows only; an empty basename becomes the literal "download". The port splits on '/' alone on every platform, because '/' is the path separator of a URL
the collision loop while (fs::exists(dest / (basename + "." + to_string(i)))) ++i; has no upper bound and probes the filesystem forever when every candidate is taken; the port stops at 10000
the download timeout is setTimeout(600), documented in the header as ten minutes
an empty download_folder becomes "./" and the destination is built by string concatenation, so the result can contain a doubled separator; Path::join names the same file without it
the header states that a partially written file is not cleaned up on write failure; the port removes it, so a failed download leaves the directory unchanged
a revision string is built from VersionInfo::getRevision(), substituting "UNKNOWN" for an empty or "exported" value, and is then never used anywhere in the function

the queried identifier is "OpenMS" + "_" + "Default_" + platform + "_" + architecture + "_" + tool_name + "_" + version, illustrated by the comment above it as OpenMS_Default_Win_64_FeatureFinderCentroided_2.0.0
the stamp file is (re)created when it is missing OR unreadable, and the touch uses a default std::ofstream, which truncates an existing unreadable file
the query happens when first_run is true or current_time > last_modified_time + 24 hours; the comparison is strict, so exactly 24 hours is not yet due

stat() and utime() bump the modification time while preserving st_atime, and this happens before the request is issued, so a failed query still consumes the day's budget; either call failing warns and continues
the notice tells the user to set OPENMS_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK to ON, but nothing in the Core SDK reads that variable; the switch is honoured by the TOPP framework in a separately versioned package
the version query uses setTimeout(5) against http://openms-update.cs.uni-tuebingen.de/check/, over plain HTTP
a server version equal to VersionDetails::EMPTY is skipped, which covers both a parse failure and a literal 0.0.0, because create() overloads one value for both
the announcement prints the local `version` argument rather than the server's version, so a user on 2.0.0 is told that version 2.0.0 is available; reproduced verbatim and reported as a C++ defect

operator< is lexicographic on (major, minor, patch) and, on a tie, ranks a version with a pre-release identifier below one without; two different identifiers on the same triple are neither less nor greater yet compare unequal, so the relation is not a strict weak ordering consistent with operator== and the port therefore does not implement PartialOrd

create() demands at least one '.', parses major, then minor up to an optional second '.', then patch up to a '-' that is searched for only after that second '.', and finally takes the remainder verbatim as the pre-release identifier; any ConversionError yields EMPTY

toInt32 skips leading space/tab/newline/carriage-return, accepts one '+', calls std::from_chars (which accepts a leading '-'), then skips trailing whitespace and throws unless the whole string was consumed

class_test_review.literal_extraction: The four default-state assertions of NetworkGetRequest_test.cpp, the 'no throw / error set / non-empty error string / empty response' shape of each of the four run() cases, the single File::exists assertion of Network_test.cpp and the two assertions of UpdateCheck_test.cpp are transcribed. The remaining expectations are derived from the implementations rather than from any test literal, and are listed under independently_derived.
not_reproduced: NetworkGetRequest_test.cpp case 3 drives CURLE_COULDNT_RESOLVE_HOST through the reserved .invalid TLD. That is a resolver call whose outcome depends on the host's DNS configuration, so the port asserts the same four properties against a recorded TransportError::HostNotFound instead.

Network_test.cpp downloads a file:// URL, which libcurl handles and ureq does not. The upstream fixture's bytes are served through a recorded transport, and the assertion is strengthened from 'the file exists' to 'the file exists at the derived name and holds exactly those bytes'.

UpdateCheck_test.cpp is #ifdef __unix__ because it redirects XDG_CONFIG_HOME with setenv. The Rust test builds the same uncreatable config directory as a FileContext value, so it needs no environment variable and runs on every platform.

independently_derived: The error boundary is exactly status >= 400: 399 is not an error and 400 is, from the .cpp comparison rather than from any test literal
The error text for a status failure is 'HTTP error 404' / 'HTTP error 503', from the source's own concatenation
A 3xx response that was not followed is not an error, by the same comparison
A timeout of 0 or any negative value leaves the request without a deadline, from the `timeout_ > 0` guard
toInt32 accepts '+-12' as -12, because the '+' is stripped before std::from_chars reads the '-'; it rejects '+ 12' and '2147483648'
VersionDetails::create rejects '1.2-alpha' - the minor component would be '2-alpha', which toInt32 refuses - while accepting '1.2.3-alpha', because the '-' is searched for only after the second '.'
'1.0.0-a'.is_greater_than('1.0.0-b') and '1.0.0-b'.is_greater_than('1.0.0-a') are both true, since operator> is !(< || ==) and neither direction of < holds
is_due is false at exactly MIN_QUERY_INTERVAL and true one second later, from the strict > in the .cpp
A failed query still consumes the 24-hour window, from the order of the utime call and the request
Three downloads of one URL produce run.tsv, run.tsv.0 and run.tsv.1, from the collision rule
'https://host' derives the file name 'host', because that is its last '/'-separated component and std::filesystem::path::filename returns it
An empty response body still produces a zero-length file, since the write is unconditional
native_boundaries: network_get_request: redirects capped at DEFAULT_MAX_REDIRECTS = 10, caller-settable up to MAX_REDIRECTS = 64, where libcurl's CURLOPT_MAXREDIRS default is unlimited
network_get_request: response body capped at DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 64 MiB, caller-settable up to MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 4 GiB, where the source's write callback appends without a ceiling
network_get_request: at most MAX_HEADERS = 1024 response headers, a bound on a native addition since the source captures no headers at all

network_get_request: UreqTransport refuses a URL without '://', with an empty host, or with a scheme other than http/https before any socket is opened, reproducing libcurl's offline CURLE_URL_MALFORMAT and CURLE_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL

network_get_request: response_text and Header::value_text return Error::InvalidValue for non-UTF-8 bytes instead of decoding lossily; the bytes stay available through response_binary and Header::value
network: URL length capped at MAX_URL_BYTES = 64 KiB, checked before a socket is opened
network: the collision-suffix search stops at MAX_NAME_SUFFIX = 10000, where the source's loop has no bound
network: a derived basename of '.', '..', or one containing '/', '\' or NUL is refused, where the source passes it to std::ofstream
network: a partially written file is removed on write failure, where the source's header states it is left behind
update_check: tool_name must be 1-256 bytes and a plain file-name component, where the source concatenates it into a path unchecked
update_check: version capped at MAX_VERSION_BYTES = 256 and the response at MAX_QUERY_RESPONSE_BYTES = 64 KiB
update_check: SemanticVersion::parse returns Option rather than the EMPTY sentinel, while should_report_update reproduces the source's `!= EMPTY` branch so the decision is unchanged
update_check: PartialOrd is deliberately not implemented, because the source's operator< disagrees with its own operator== for two distinct pre-release identifiers
network_isolation: No test in this group opens a socket. The two malformed-URL cases of NetworkGetRequest_test.cpp go through the real UreqTransport, whose URL preflight refuses them before any connection is attempted; every other case uses a recorded HttpTransport implemented in the test file. In particular nothing queries http://openms-update.cs.uni-tuebingen.de, which would report the build machine's usage to an upstream server.
openmp: None of the four headers or their implementations carries a #pragma omp, so there is no parallel behaviour to match and no performance gap to record for this group.

external_dependency.note: Already a declared, non-default dependency of the crate before this port; no dependency was added. Its default features (rustls, gzip) are in effect. Nothing outside src/system/network_get_request.rs names it.
